fatal_errors: The response mistakes high-entropy alloys, a class of materials, for the processing method sought by the question.
It omits the central high-energy ball milling plus spark plasma sintering intervention and all defining process conditions.
It predicts enhanced ductility and corrosion resistance without target-specific support; the target instead reports limited ductility and intergranular fracture.
The proposed experiment compares broad alloy classes rather than testing how milling and sintering control phase fractions, grain size, densification, and mechanical properties.
explanation: The hypothesis is only broadly aligned with multicomponent alloys and improved mechanical properties. It does not reconstruct the operative method—argon high-energy ball milling followed by vacuum spark plasma sintering—or the relevant milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, time, temperature, heating rate, and hold time. Its simple-crystal-structure explanation misses the nanocrystalline mixed FCC/BCC structure and the combined Hall–Petch, dislocation, solid-solution, and densification mechanisms. The cited evidence supports generic claims about HEAs but not the specific processing route, phase stability, quantitative outcomes, or process boundaries. The proposed falsification study is measurable but cannot discriminate the target processing mechanism.
